neighbours.label: support giving way beneath someone: footing lost from under (out from under, gave way, slipped underneath)
fire: The ladder slid sideways and the rungs went out from under him.
Halfway across the frozen pond, the ice gave way and she dropped into the water.
The rotten floorboards collapsed beneath his weight and he fell into the cellar.
Her knees buckled and the ground seemed to vanish from under her feet.
As the riverbank crumbled, the soil slipped away underneath the old fence post.
The rope snapped and the bridge planks fell out from under the hikers.
When the chair leg broke, the seat dropped out from under the speaker mid-sentence.
The scaffolding gave way and two workers tumbled onto the pavement below.
quiet: The ladder stood firmly against the wall while he painted the window frame.
Halfway across the frozen pond, she stopped to watch the skaters under the lights.
The old floorboards creaked under his weight as he walked into the cellar.
Her cat likes to sleep under the bed when guests come to visit.
Along the riverbank, wild mint grows underneath the old fence posts.
The hikers rested on the bridge and looked at the river below.
The speaker sat on a chair under the tent and read from his notes.
The scaffolding stood beside the church for two years during the repairs.

notes: Opposite pole is sheltered 'under a canopy'; the distinction is losing vs having support/cover beneath.
